references.text: Joshua is appointed as the one who will lead Israel into the promised land, just as in Deuteronomy 3:28.
Moses gives Joshua strength and courage, and commands him to lead the people into the land, as a direct fulfillment of the command in 3:28.
The Lord Himself strengthens Joshua and confirms that he will lead the people into the land, using the same words about being strong and courageous.
Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor and given authority to lead the people, preparing for the fulfillment of the command in Deuteronomy 3:28.
Joshua receives God's command to be strong and courageous and to lead the people across the Jordan to take possession of the land, fulfilling what Moses was commanded in 3:28.
Joshua completed the task of distributing the land as an inheritance to the tribes, fulfilling the prophecy in Deuteronomy 3:28.
Joshua is first mentioned as Moses' chosen leader in battle, showing his early role as military leader for the people.
Refers to Joshua leading the people into rest, but points to a greater rest that still remains through Jesus.
